_comment: Asset contract: every mesh the city data places, with size, pivot and axes. Keys match Set/Kind in out/<city>/pcg/*.csv and ue5/Config/asset_map.json. Sizes are metres at Scale 1. Generated prompts: tools/asset_prompts.py. Delivered files are checked by tools/check_assets.py.

conventions.units: metres in source files (glTF), centimetres after UE import
conventions.forward: UE +X is the 'forward' named in each entry; yaw in the CSV turns +X to the given direction
conventions.naming: SM_<set>_<kind>_v<n> for props, SM_<archetype>_<module>_v<n> for kits; textures T_<name>_{BaseColor,Normal,ORM}
conventions.materials: PBR metal/rough, ORM packed (R occlusion, G roughness, B metallic)
conventions.texel_density: ~512 px/m for props near the player, 256 px/m for facades and large props
conventions.lods: Nanite for opaque meshes marked nanite=true; others need LOD0-LOD2 (100/50/25%)
conventions.file_format: glTF 2.0 binary (.glb), one asset per file, pivot as specified, applied transforms
conventions.licence: every file needs an entry in game/assets/sources.json (source, author, licence, url)
conventions.axes: Same frame as the city tiles. In Blender: +X = the entry's 'forward', +Z up (Blender +Y becomes UE -Y). In the .glb (exported '+Y up'): +X forward, +Y up, +Z = UE +Y. tools/check_assets.py reads the glb in this frame. If the first UE import shows props turned, fix it once with yaw_offset_deg in ue5/Config/asset_map.json.
conventions.route: generate = imagegen ref sheet -> image-to-3D -> cleanup; hand = Blender/PCG/spline; hand_vegetation = UE Procedural Vegetation Editor or Blender with photographed bark/leaf; reuse_or_hand = CC0/CC-BY model if one fits (docs/08), else hand; hand_mesh_generated_print = simple frame mesh, generated background print, text rendered in UE. Kits are hand-modelled on the module grid.

kit_rules.module_axes: front face on the X=0 plane facing +X; module runs from Y=0 to Y=width; base at Z=0. Balconies and signs may stick out up to +1.2 m in X, walls go back to -0.3 m
kit_rules.widths: the PCG kit picks the widest module set that fits each frontage edge from semantics/footprints_*.json, then fills the rest with smaller ones
kit_rules.ground_floor: shopfront edges get ground_* modules; other street edges get mid_* modules at ground level
